subject: Food Science
title: Foodborne Illness Investigation
description: A quick win: understand Foodborne Illness Investigation.

hook.text: A wedding dinner sickens 60 guests with Salmonella. Investigators must determine which dish, ingredient, and supplier caused it.

buildup.text: Case-control studies compare what sick people ate versus what healthy attendees ate. Statistical differences point to the culprit.

discovery.text: Traceback follows the food from plate to kitchen to distributor to farm. Each link is verified with invoices and shipping records.

twist.text: Sometimes the source is never found. Complex supply chains, mixed ingredients, and delayed reporting create dead ends.

climax.text: Environmental sampling of the kitchen—swabbing surfaces, drains, and equipment—often proves contamination pathways.

punchline.text: Compare the sick and the healthy. The food they don't share is the suspect.

quiz.question: How do case-control studies identify the source food?
options: By comparing what sick people ate versus what healthy attendees ate
